entries.title: James 3:1
segments: My brothers, do not be many teachers, knowing that we shall receive the greater condemnation.

entries.title: James 3:2
segments: For [in] many [things] we all offend. If anyone does not offend in word, the same [is] a full-grown man, able also to bridle the whole body.

entries.title: James 3:3
segments: Behold, we put bits in the horses' mouths, so that they may obey us, and we turn about their whole body.

entries.title: James 3:4
segments: Behold also the ships being so great, and driven by fierce winds, yet they are turned about with a very small rudder, where the impulse of him steering desires.

entries.title: James 3:5
segments: Even so the tongue is a little member and boasts great things. Behold how little a fire kindles how large a forest!

entries.title: James 3:6
segments: And the tongue [is] a fire, a world of iniquity. So the tongue is set among our members, spotting all the body and inflaming the course of nature, and being inflamed by hell.

entries.title: James 3:7
segments: For every kind of animals, and of birds, and of reptiles, and of sea-animals, is tamed, and has been tamed by mankind.

entries.title: James 3:8
segments: But no one can tame the tongue, [it is] an unruly evil, full of deadly poison.

entries.title: James 3:9
segments: By this we bless God, even [the] Father. And by this we curse men, who have come into being according to the image of God.

entries.title: James 3:10
segments: Out of the same mouth proceeds blessing and cursing. My brothers, these things ought not to be so.

entries.title: James 3:11
segments: Does a fountain send forth at the same hole the sweet and the bitter?

entries.title: James 3:12
segments: Can the fig tree, my brothers, bear olive berries; or a vine, figs? So no fountain [can] yield both salt water and fresh.

entries.title: James 3:13
segments: Who [is] wise and knowing among you? Let him show his works by [his] good conduct with meekness of wisdom.

entries.title: James 3:14
segments: But if you have bitter jealousy and strife in your hearts, do not glory and lie against the truth.

entries.title: James 3:15
segments: This is not the wisdom coming down from above, but [is] earthly, sensual, devilish.

entries.title: James 3:16
segments: For where envying and strife [are], there [is] confusion and every foul deed.

entries.title: James 3:17
segments: But the wisdom that is from above is first truly pure, then peaceable, gentle, easy to be entreated, full of mercy and good fruits, without partiality and without hypocrisy.

entries.title: James 3:18
segments: And [the] fruit of righteousness is sown in peace by those who make peace.
